utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We'll first conclude the evidence of this witness. Meanwhile, I remind the parties that on the 23rd of June the Chamber has stated that it wishes to be provided with a map containing various positions mentioned by Witness Milos Skrba in particular the Gugina Kucar [phoen] crossroads and a feature called number 8, Osmica, in order to better understand the witness's testimony. And the Prosecution indicated that it would further endeavour to get additional information, and the Chamber wondered whether the Prosecution is in a position to provide the Chamber with the map containing the necessary information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Your Honours. We have located -- we do have the location for this Osmica. We are not able to locate the other place yet. And if we could be given until the end of today to respond to Your Honours, perhaps we could meet with Mr. -- well, with the Defence counsel as well to see if they could assist in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That request is granted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Tusevljak.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I would like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you have given at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Shin will now -- yes, and that is one. We also do understand that you have brought the document we asked you to bring with you. Perhaps, Mr. Usher, could you already receive that document from the witness so that the Chamber and the parties can have a look at it. Meanwhile, Mr. Shin will continue his cross-examination. Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Tusevljak.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, yesterday when we left off we were discussing the 60-millimetre mortars in your company, and we were dealing with paragraph 13 in your Karadzic statement. And I'm going to read it to you in its entirety since we have it only in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Could I please have the document assigned to D540 brought up on the screen. And if we could please turn to the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: We'll wait until it's up. Actually, since it's going to be in translation for you, Mr. Tusevljak, I'll just begin reading it. "When the SRK was formed, my unit was named the 1st Platoon of the 4th Company of the 2nd Battalion of the 1st Smbr, and we held the same positions until the end of the war. We only had one mortar but no mortar bombs." Now, Mr. Tusevljak, the language of that paragraph, it's simple and it's clear; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: When I asked you further questions, you first stated that by the word "we" you meant the company not the platoon, and you said "that's another error" in your statement. Now, you said that was an error because you knew that anyone reading this -- these two sentences would naturally be confused and think that you were talking about your platoon. That's why you said that's another error; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they belong to the company, to the -- these two mortars. That was part of the company. As a platoon, we didn't have any mortars. The company command was above us, and behind the company HQ was that mortar. It was set up higher. Actually, in a valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Tusevljak, you said that this was another error in your statement because you knew that somebody reading this would, of course, think that you were talking about the platoon. That's my question to you. That is why you said this was an error in your statement.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We, as a platoon, we didn't have -- I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- it's an error. Perhaps when I said "we," I meant the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes. And then on further questioning, you agreed that the company did not "only have one" mortar but that it had two. That's what you said; correct? You remember that.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And on even further questions you were even willing to say that it was possibly three mortars; right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible. I said I didn't know. I know that one was operational. As for the others, they were not used. Perhaps they were not operating, something about the sights. I think that's what the crew of the mortars told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Tusevljak, please listen carefully to my question. Now your statement said we only had one mortar, and already now you're willing to admit the possibility of three; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I said "one," I meant the one that was in working order. The others, one or two, they were not in working order. That's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Then when I asked you about this phrase "no mortar bombs," you told this Court that all you meant by that was that there were no mortar shells on one day, the 8th of June, 1992, out of a four-year war - one day you say your company had no mortar shells; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the 8th of June we didn't have any. They were needed. We asked for mortar fire from that one, but they said they didn't have any shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And you would agree with me that in your Karadzic statement, as we discussed yesterday, there is nothing to indicate the limitation of that phrase "no mortar bombs" to just one day out of the entire war. There is nothing in your statement that does that, is there?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. That's how it was written. That's how it was formulated. I know what I meant to say, but as for the way it was put, it's not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Tusevljak, that's the way it was written and that's the way you signed it. That's the way you signed that statement.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now in light of the changes, when we look again at paragraph 13 of your Karadzic statement, isn't it clear that anyone reading that paragraph would be misled in their understanding about the situation regarding mortars in your company?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Your Honours, I think that this is the third time that one and the same question is being repeated to which the witness already replied yesterday and today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: What was the witness's answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think that the problem is, Mr. Stojanovic, that the witness is not properly answering the question. So, therefore, then you can put it again to the witness. Please proceed, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Tusevljak, do you need the question again?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So what's your answer? Anyone reading that would be misled about the situation regarding mortars in your company. That's obvious; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: -- knowing that someone reading that would be misled, you said nothing. You said nothing when you signed this statement. You said nothing during proofing, you said nothing here in Court until I started asking you questions about this. In fact, on Wednesday when Defence counsel asked you "does this" these statements, "fully correspond to what you wish to say, what you did say, and what your recollection is," that was another opportunity for you to correct this misleading impression that your statement had left; isn't that correct? That was another opportunity. Just tell me. It's correct that this was another opportunity to do -- to make this correction?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it's correct. But again, I'm not a lawyer. I didn't really understand properly that that would mean something else other than what I meant to talk about. That it can be interpreted differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Tusevljak --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Shin, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's [indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now yesterday, Mr. Tusevljak, before we finished you acknowledged -- or before we finished, you said about the 8th of June 1992, you said: "There were a few shells, most of them were incendiary but on the 8th we didn't have any. These were just used to light up the sky at night." Now, Mr. Tusevljak, incendiary shells, they are used to set their targets on fire. That's what they're for; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, incendiary ones. But I didn't know that they had incendiary ones for mortars. They were illuminating ones which would light up the area at night. I knew that some sort of action was being prepared so we would observe what was going on, but on the evening of the 7th of June they used three or four of those shells which are illuminating ones. They don't have any other function.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: They also had regular shells, the kind that explode on impact?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think there were a few of them up there at that command before that. I think that there were some, but I don't know how many. All I can remember is that on the 7th in the evening we were firing -- actually, they were firing the tracing ones so that we could observe positions. You could hear the sound of trucks, preparations for the attack, probably, so we asked for this area to be illuminated. We didn't have any, actually. I asked for fire to be executed in front of our positions. We didn't have any shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: You didn't know how many shells, so you can't really say that they had very few shells. You've just told us that you didn't know.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was up there during those days, I think that there was a box. Next to that there was another box with these tracer shells. I saw that. I was talking with these guys and they said only that one was functional and that was the only one that could fire, and that's why I think that there wasn't a lot. It wasn't a depot. It was in the field, it was covered with tent material, water proof material, but it's not up to me. It's not my job to know how many of these things they had. Probably on the 8th they didn't have any.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: We'll return to that issue of the mortar shells. Now let's just go to the structure of your company. It's correct that there were four infantry platoons; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: There was also a scouts or a reconnaissance section; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't a special squad or something. It was a young man who would go somewhere where it would be better -- there would be a better position to observe the positions in front of us. There was no particular surveillance or reconnaissance units. Somebody would get a task to go, have a look, come back to the lines, so that they could at least get a look at what was in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Tusevljak --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no squad --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: -- maybe I --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- as such. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Please focus on my questions, and if I feel that you're going astray, I may indicate that you're going beyond the scope of the question. Now, apart from the 60-millimetre mortars, were there any other mortars in the company?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. I didn't see it. I know that this 60 was close by, but I don't know about anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So during your four years with the company, as far as you know, is your evidence that there was no other mortar apart from the 60-millimetre mortars in your company?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. I think that behind the company quite a distance away in the depth there was a mortar unit that also provided support fire for us, and that's where they had five or six mortars. I don't know what kind. But I know that they were deep in the depth of the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to turn to a different topic now. In your statement for this case in paragraph 2, you state: "There was one sniper in my platoon and it was actually a sniper that belonged to the battalion according to the establishment."

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And it's not on this document, so we won't need it on the screen. It's the other document, D539. But let's stay with this document, because I will be returning to it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Tusevljak, in your Karadzic statement on paragraph 26 --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And that's E4 -- and that's page 4 on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: -- you mention that at the end of 1993 a trained sniper was sent to your unit. Now, my first question to you is: Are we talking about the same person or is this someone different? So in your Mladic statement you mention that there was one sniper in your platoon; in your Karadzic statement you mention that at the end of 1993 a sniper was sent to your unit. The same person or different people?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same person. It was that one and only person that came then. It's the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: What was this person's name?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me when I say that I don't know. He was not part of our company. He was sent either from the battalion or the brigade, and we complained to the battalion commander that we couldn't work around in that area because of the sniper from the other side, and then he sent somebody to try to neutralise the other sniper.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And, in fact, a sniper is an effective way to eliminate a sniper; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that a sniper would work against a sniper. Then it's better to do it that way, for him to find him and neutralise him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, you've told this Court that --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And that's paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Well, you've told this Court that there were 230 members of your unit who were killed during the war, and you said that: "They were killed in fighting. Most of them were killed in sniper fire." Now, you, as a platoon leader, you're responsible for the safety of your men; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So given the scope and scale of what you say is a sniper fire against you, it would be natural for you to ask for snipers to counter that sniper fire; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In this case we asked about Asimovo Brdo, but there were snipers from the town as well. They would fire at us all along the street, at our company, directly. The sniper from Asimovo Brdo that was opposite us, he was able to have an overview from the command to Banjalucka Street, and that's why we asked for the command for a way to deal with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So, Mr. Tusevljak, is this the -- this time at the end of 1993 when a sniper was sent to you, was that the only time you asked for a sniper or did you ask for a sniper on more occasions?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We asked for it before, a couple of times either a sniper or some weapon. We knew more or less where the two houses were from where the sniper was shooting from Asimovo Brdo, but they didn't have anybody to send to us, so then later they sent this man.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now in your Karadzic statement at paragraph 26, the document that we have on the screen, you say that after this sniper was killed by a Muslim sniper: "After this, no other snipers arrived." And you've just explained that. You also say: "I also know for a fact that the neighbouring platoons did not have any snipers in their ranks." First of all, by "neighboring platoons" you're talking about the other three platoons in your company; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were to the left and to the right of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So is your testimony, then, that there were no snipers at all in your company?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. There were none. Had there been any, then they wouldn't have needed to send somebody from the brigade or the battalion. I don't know where he came from. But in any event, he was sent by the battalion command.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Let me put a slightly different question to you. Isn't it true that soldiers in your company used sniper rifles?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps in the company, yes, but these were these old snipers. We had one at the company command. Somebody could take the sniper rifle and use it if they needed it. We couldn't use it because we were so close by and nobody could be effective against such a precise sniper who fired at Ozrenska and at us. He was a good sniper shooter and nobody could deal with that, so we practically didn't use the sniper rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So your evidence is that there was only one sniper rifle in your company. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there was one. I saw one at the command. I didn't read there if there were any more, but I think I only saw that one at the command of the company in the racks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. We're now going to go look at some documents, and these documents pertain to weapons in your company.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Could I please have 65 ter 30867.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tusevljak, while we're waiting for this to come up on this -- on the screen, let me explain to you what it is. It's a document from the 2nd Battalion, 4th Company - your company - and it's dated the 22nd of October, 1993. We see that in the upper left-hand corner now. And we also see the location Ozrenska. That would be Ozrenska Street; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Ozrenska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And at the bottom --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: It's the second page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: -- you see that it's signed by Mr. Major Dragutin Loncaric. We've already discussed who he is. Now you see a reference to the Zbrojevka Brno rifle -- or weapon. We've discussed that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we go back to the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, the first page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And that's the fourth item there. A little further down we see references to two M-84s, we talked about that. You told us about an effective range if you had an optical sight for that. And by the way, that weapon was also referred to as the sower of death, right, "sejac smrti"?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And likewise we find references to M-48s, a weapon we discussed yesterday. Now starting at line 6 -- so going back near the top of this, just before -- just under the letter PAN, we see the entry MB-60 mm; that is a 60-millimetre mortar. And we see that appearing three times. So that means there are three 60-millimetre mortars; correct? Are we clear on that now?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And we also see just below that MB-82 mm. That is an 82-millimetre mortar; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So, in fact, the company had an additional mortar and it was an 82-millimetre mortar; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never seen it. I saw the one I mentioned already. Perhaps it was not in operation at the time. And the other two, I've never seen them. It was somewhere further away. I am not aware of the 82-millimetre piece ever engaging anything, too. I don't even know whether it was there at all. Perhaps it's just on the list. I'm not familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Tusevljak, we'll see some other documents pertaining to that. But your evidence right now is that during your four years you had no knowledge that an 82-millimetre mortar was ever engaged; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think I saw it at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: We also see further down a reference to -- and I think it's the -- or it's the bottom of the page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I believe it's the second page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: We see a reference to two Osa. Yes, there it is. Now, an Osa that's a portable rocket launcher, multi-use; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Osa is portable but it has a single tube. It has one rocket that can be used to engage tanks, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And we also see at the bottom --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And back on page 1 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: -- that there are two weapons listed as broving, and those are browning machine-guns of different calibres; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution would tender 30867.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30867 receives number P6624, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6624 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, can I please have 65 ter 30868 brought up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tusevljak, while we're waiting for that to come up, I'll explain what it is. It's a document from the 4th Infantry Company, 2nd Battalion. Again, the location is Ozrenska we see on the upper left, and it's dated the 3rd of December, 1993. Now we see that it's signed by Lieutenant Dusan Zurovac for the commander. We've heard about him already. He's a supply officer at the 4th Company's command. Now, we see that he's requesting various ammunition, including one crate of 60-millimetre shells and two crates of 82-millimetre shells. That would suggest that the 82-millimetre mortar was used; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I don't know. I only know about the 60-millimetre pieces. I'm not aware of the whereabouts of the 82-millimetre piece. I guess it was there, but we were further down. I've no clue. I never asked for anything of the sort. I didn't even know there was one. I only knew of the 60-millimetre piece. I'm not aware of this one. Maybe it was lent. The pieces were carried around all the time. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution would tender 30868.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, I'd like -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30868 receives number P6625, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6625 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to continue on with another document. But before doing that, if Your Honours would permit, I would like to pass out a hard copy of what is currently D545 because I would like the witness to compare that with what's going to be on the screen in B/C/S and in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections I take, Mr. Stojanovic. We --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: We have copies available, of course, for -- the Defence can find it on the screen. But we have hard copies available for the Defence and for Your Honours when we go through this process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed as you suggested, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Now could we please have on the screen 65 ter 30865. And we'll take a moment and just wait for that document to come up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tusevljak, if we look at the document on the screen, if you look on the left you see that it's a handwritten document. And I'm going to go to some specific pages first before we consider this document as a whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Can we first go to page in the English 4 and the B/C/S 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN

utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.text: Document 30865 receives number P6626, Your Honours.

utterances.text: P6626 is admitted.

utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tusevljak, we're going to go to a few other places in this -- in this notebook.

utterances.text: Yes. No, I'm sorry --

utterances.text: Do you see, Mr. Tusevljak, the line that says: "Mortar Section, two cases, shells for an 82-millimetre mortar, received by Lj. Bozic"?

utterances.text: And if we could now go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I don't think that was your evidence, but we'll continue now. And we'll just go through a couple more of these because the Judges have this document now and there are other issues that can be examined.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Let's turn to page 9 in both the English and the B/C/S. And it's on the right-hand side, I believe, of both languages at the top.

utterances.text: I would like to turn to another document, please. Could I please have document 65 ter 30864.

utterances.text: Yes. The page we are looking at now is 1995, Witness, whereas the previous pages were from spring 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: That's correct. So I guess -- the -- the contrast now is quite clear. If I could please have 65 -- yes, we have that now. And I would ask to go to English page 5 and B/C/S page 4. Yes.

utterances.text: Now we see that this is a document from the 2nd Infantry Battalion, 4th Company. Again, Ozrenska. The date is the 15th of January, 1994. The document - we needn't go to the signature page - it's signed by Dusan Zurovac.

utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.text: Now, the Tandzara, which we discussed yesterday, that has an effective range of over 1000 metres with a scope; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]

utterances.text: And if we turn now to the next page in the B/C/S and stay on this page in English and number 39.

utterances.text: We see a reference to "sniper."

utterances.text: Under the -- after the name Savic, Blagoje, we see this phrase, "... sniper, M-48 with optical sight." Mr. Tusevljak, this does show that there were snipers in your company or individuals using sniper weapons; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it in the documents but I wasn't aware of it. This documentation dates back to April and May 1992. At the time the war hadn't even gun yet. I don't know what people purchased up there or had at Ozrenska. I know that this guy, for example, was some kind of company commander so perhaps he had to make a list. But later on when I became commander of the 2nd Platoon, these were no longer used. I didn't have it. The one we did was up with the company. I never saw anyone coming to my positions with the -- a sniper rifle. Indeed, there was no need for it. However, this was at the very beginning. That's how I see this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: Was there any reason why we did not look at 89 - and that's my first question. And the second question is whether you could take the witness and the Chamber --

utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: -- back to the date of this document.

utterances.text: And to be fair to you, Mr. Tusevljak, perhaps we went quickly past this, but I think the date is clearer there. And it is for January 15th, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And, yes, Your Honours, there are -- there will be other information that's relevant in all these documents, but in the interest of time I have cut short some of those parts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So you see the date, Mr. Tusevljak?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see it now. But a moment ago I saw a document dated back in April or May where there was some reference to a sniper. But, for example, this document, Cero Rajko [phoen]. utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Given the last response by the witness to the effect that Rajko, Cero, was killed, I think it would be only fair to the witness to show him the title of this document to see what is asked for in the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you could have done so in re-examination if you wished to do. You can object against questions. Although I must add to that that sometimes in obvious situations it may sometimes be appreciated if there is any assistance. I do not know whether this is such an occasion. I leave that in Mr. Shin's hands. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honour. Just one sentence. The questions were in the context of the fact of -- if the unit had snipers at this particular date, but the heading of the document perhaps could provide an answer. That's why I spoke out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, do you understand English? Do you understand English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you take your earphones off for a second. Mr. Stojanovic, you are entering into a debate on what, as we see in English, "claimed weapons" means. Now, if I claim a weapon and I have already the numbers of the weapons there, there are two ways of understanding "claimed weapons," those that were claimed and received and those that are still claimed and have not yet been received. Now please explain to me why you have already the serial numbers of the weapons you have not yet received. That is a discussion which can take place but not as an intervention in the examination by Mr. Shin. I hope that before you do it again, you think it over twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And just on that - and I don't wish to engage into an argument - but the document itself indicates what the status of some of these individuals are, and I'll leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Apart from that, sometimes handwriting adds to the information which suggests that it's updated regularly and --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And therefore for three or four reasons, Mr. Stojanovic, it would have been better to think it over twice before you intervened. And I again repeat that sometimes in obvious cases, and apparently this is not such an obvious case, that it can be appreciated but be very careful with that. Mr. Shin, you may proceed after the witness has put on his earphones again. Svedok, Witness. The witness even doesn't understand my B/C/S. That is problematic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but if I say please proceed, Mr. Shin, I'm also looking at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I would need five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Five minutes. Then I would suggest that we continue for five minutes, take the break, and that the witness would be re-examined after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Could I tender this document, please. This is 65 ter 30864.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30864 receives number P6627, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6627 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I would like to turn to a -- 65 ter 30869.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution would tender 30869.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30869 receives number P6628, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: -- photograph is a photograph taken from Ozrenska Street towards the location of the incident, sniping incident F4. We'll be looking at a zoomed-in picture next.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was exactly what was missing when you tendered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because line of sight, line of sight by the millions in this worlds, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, my apologies. I'm hurrying a little which is not wise.

utterances.text: No, no. Witness, do you confirm that this is a picture from Ozrenska Street to the place where incident F4 happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, sir. I see the place, but this is all the way to the right from my positions. I was all the way to the left. From this part you could see it. utterances.text: But this was under the control of your armed forces, wasn't it?

utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not quite sure whether this place was held by our company or the neighboring company. But, yes, all the way down to Grbavica. I'm not sure which company.

utterances.text: That's the reason why I used the expression "armed forces." One second please, Mr. Shin. P6628 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.text: And one final document. If we could please have 65 ter 30870.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution would tender 30870.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30870 receives number P6629, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6629 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And a final question for you, Mr. Tusevljak. You were explaining to the Judges that this was not held by your company. utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. My platoon was all the way to the left, far away. This is either at the very end of the AOR of my company and the beginning of the AOR of the next company. utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- driver's hole, so it wasn't possible to see this place from where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- they were uploaded separately and without 65 ter numbers. That's what needs to be done in order to achieve what you wish to achieve. We take a break and will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, while we're waiting perhaps I could just address the Osmica issue and indicate where we believe it is and perhaps we could hear more from the Defence on where it may be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you do that already among yourself and then if you agree that we receive your shared opinion about it, and if there is any disagreement then, of course, the Chamber --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- would hear where you think it is --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and where Mr. Stojanovic thinks it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Of course, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tusevljak, you will now be re-examined by Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Stojanovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tusevljak, when you spoke with this Defence during proofing for your testimony, did you also talk about the fact that your platoon did have a sniper which was from the battalion?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we now look at document D539, please. Could we look at paragraph 2 of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It is written here that you said: "In my platoon, there was one sniper and that was the sniper that belonged to the battalion by establishment." Is that what you said when asked by Mr. Shin that you told us?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I did say that that was in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And can you explain to the Trial Chamber what does it mean "belonged to the battalion by establishment" and not to your platoon?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that that sniper was not issued to anyone. It was recorded as its sniper. The battalion commander issued a sniper rifle so that we could use it. We were not issued one in our platoon and that is why it was recorded and at the company command.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at document D545.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, have I misunderstood something? Isn't it that Mr. Shin mainly focused on the presence of snipers in the company and that asking questions about a platoon or battalion doesn't resolve that that much? Because battalion is not company, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I just wanted to complete these questions regarding his platoon and the possession of sniper rifles pursuant to his own statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this is what I wanted to ask you, Witness. This is a list of weaponry of the 1st Platoon of the 4th Company. And you had the opportunity to see this list. Could you please tell me: Are you able to answer according to your best recollection when -- what is the period of this list?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I think this is a list from 1993, late 1993. I'm not here so that means that I probably moved to the other platoon. Or it could be 1994. I cannot remember exactly. This is after I moved. I'm not on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then when you see this, and based on what you know about weapons, could any of these weapons in the 1st Platoon of the 4th Company be described as a sniper rifle?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so, because these two rifles, M-48s, we used them. They were modified. The mouth of the barrel was modified. There was a kind of a shape made so that you could use it to fire bombs. The PM machine-guns, they didn't have any optical sights -- actually, they did but it was in a case at the command. We didn't really need that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say they were not needed because of the distance, what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I am thinking of the enemy lines in front of us. They were so close that we didn't need to use any optical sights. It was very close and the machine-guns were placed between houses where there was a clearing, so they were at those locations. We couldn't see the town away, farther away from us because there were these houses that were right there in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I am going to end with questions relating to those two photographs. Do you recognise the position or that place and those houses where that photograph was taken which you said was part of Ozrenska Street?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recognise the houses. But just based on my recollection, it's possible that quite a distance to the right of us, that's where it was. You could see some street. This is possible that it's from some section of Ozrenska Street to the right, but I don't know it for a fact. I don't recognise the houses because that was far away from where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And did you personally have any information that the platoon or company that was right next to you were using sniper rifles?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I didn't go there. We had enough problems in our own platoon so that we never went to those other positions. I didn't know anything about that. I didn't know anything about whether there were any snipers or sharpshooters there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now that after the examination-in-chief and the cross-examination you pointed to the possible interpretations and factographical mistakes, do you stand by what you said in these two statements in their entirety?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I do. I stand by everything I said according to my recollection except for those amendments or changes that were probably made.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, Your Honours, I'm going to finish with the following suggestion because I was notified that the redacted version of document which is MFI D540 has now been uploaded into e-court with the remark that the document that was redacted has the 65 ter marking 1D02065A. And can we please ask for the documents to be entered into e-court as Exhibit D540?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have a look at it first.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I was simply going to ask if we could look at it first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we go through the pages one by one. We don't have to look, only if we arrive at a page where we find -- and I think it's paragraph 25. If we arrive at the page where the -- we expect the -- yes. Next page, please. There we are. Let's have a look. Yes. The reference to further elaboration on F10 is skipped. Here is redacted. Last page, please. Yes. Madam Registrar -- and let's just check. What you showed to us is 1D02065A. Madam Registrar, you may replace the document which is at present under MFI D540 by the one just shown to, that's 1D02065A. Do we have a translation yet with the redaction? Or I should ask for the original, as a matter of fact, because -- yes, the English version is signed. Has the original been redacted as well, Mr. Stojanovic? If not, I think if we clearly put on the record that the redacted portion in the English language is not in evidence and therefore we can ignore whatever remains in the B/C/S version. Under those circumstances, Madam Registrar, you may replace the English version by the new one. And D540 is admitted into evidence. Any further questions, Mr. Shin?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: No further questions. Just one matter. We have the witness's original --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Has it been shown to the Defence? As a matter of fact, I have instructed that it be shown to the parties. I take it that you have inspected the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, we've looked at it and we don't have any questions arising from it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may just ask: I didn't receive the translation of the last couple of words, so I couldn't really follow what Mr. Shin said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Shin wondered what to do with the document that was handed over by the witness, and he also explained to us that he has no further question in relation to this. I then said that I had given the instruction to show it to both parties for inspection. The Chamber has no further questions on it. Do you have any further questions in relation to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, please, with the assistance of the usher, give it back to the witness. Mr. Usher, could you please assist. Mr. Tusevljak, the Chamber appreciated very much that you have brought the document. It's returned to you now. This also concludes your evidence in this court. I would like to thank you very much for having come to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you, questions put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before I invite the Defence to call its next witness, I would like to deal with a few procedural matters. One of them I dealt with already, that was the statement of Mr. Lalovic, D498. Has the document been uploaded in [indiscernible] yet or not yet? I said something about it before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. And I received information that it has been uploaded, this number for the statement of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I gave some comments on the way in which it was uploaded. Has this been corrected, Mr. Stojanovic? Because it was uploaded separately without 65 ter numbers where it should be jointly uploaded with a 65 ter number?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I confirm that I --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I received it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And it's been uploaded at the same 65 ter number with the additional suffix a.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: So it's uploaded as 1D01650A, 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, you may replace the newly uploaded document -- no, you may replace the old document with the newly uploaded one. That was one matter. Yes, was it MFI'd, Madam Registrar? It was.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It was MFI'd, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then it's hereby also admitted. D498 is admitted into evidence. For the next item, we briefly turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We'll now take the time to deal with the scheduling of witnesses until the summer recess. Mr. Groome, you asked to reserve time for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And Ms. Bibles will deal with this matter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have received or we have received the list of Defence proposed witnesses to the end of the break. We had provided a list of witnesses that we would not object to; i.e., they -- for example, they fell within our agreement or they did not fall within the agreement but we agreed they could come. My quick review of the list reveals that most of the witnesses are fine but there are two witnesses that we would object to. They have not testified previously. I'll address that with the Defence team at the next break, and I think at that point then we can probably give better advice to the Trial Chamber and prepare the issue better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we'll then wait for you -- well, later this morning. There is one issue, the two witnesses, GRM159 and 158, they are both scheduled for the 14th of July. Are they among the ones -- I remember that there was some discussion as to whether there would be need to cross-examine them at all but that depended on a further agreement on skipping or at least doing something with part of their statements. I think it had to do with relevance or tu quoque issues. Now, has that been resolved? Because on this list we see that no time is reserved for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: That's accurate, Your Honour. The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The matter has been resolved?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: The matter has not been resolved. I believe, as the Chamber may recall, we had suggested that these may be appropriate for 92 bis consideration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: But we have discussed the matter. We have advised that at this point based on the statements alone there would not be cross-examination. There may be -- if there was cross-examination, it would be very, very small with respect to one witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you further see whether you could reach an agreement on whether to make these witnesses 92 bis witnesses where the Prosecution apparently has not much to deal with in cross-examination. Mr. Lukic, has the Defence made up its mind already on the matter or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do not have resources as the Prosecution has, so for us it's not that easy to organise all the witnesses and to contact them. I was just informed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yeah, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- a few seconds ago that two witnesses from this list we provided this morning cannot be here, because we were not able to contact them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Mr. Lukic, you're dealing with other matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But to change a Rule 92 ter witness into a 92 bis witness does not take much time. You just have to tell them, You don't have to come and the statement which needs to be taken anyhow, 92 ter, 92 bis, it has to be signed anyhow. The only thing is the attestation. It doesn't take any more than that. So I was focusing exclusively on GRM158 and 159. And I think I announced that we would further hear from the parties after the next break once they had sat together with coffee or tea.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the Chamber, to the extent possible, would like to be informed further with the matter with GRM158 and 159 would have been resolved, at least as far as the Defence is concerned, because I can imagine that even if the attestation would not be received before the 14th of July, if the witness becomes a 92 bis witness then we are not in a hurry. It could well be done in August or September or whenever because the witness doesn't have to come to The Hague. I should say the witnesses. Then having dealt with that, I don't think that I have any other procedural issue at this moment which means that we could invite the Defence to call its next witness. The next witness would be? Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sinisa Maksimovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: There is -- I have 55 words that might eliminate a procedural issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. 55 words. I'll count them. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, on 10 June at transcript 22452, I asked for additional time to provide further submissions on the admission of two statements currently MFI'd as P6585 and P6586. At this time I withdraw my motion for admission while we explore other avenues of presenting the relevant substance of these statements into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Bibles. It doesn't come as a surprise because it was announced already. Madam Registrar, P6585 and P6586 are vacated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Maksimovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence, Mr. Maksimovic, the Rules require that you make the solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is handed out to you. I would like to invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated Mr. Maksimovic. Mr. Maksimovic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Stojanovic. You'll find him to your left. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. You may proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, for the record, kindly tell us your first and last name slowly.

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Sinisa Maksimovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness be asked to approach the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you come a bit closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The interpreters have difficulties hearing you. Witness, you -- you said "okay," was that because you understood my English or it was interpreted to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you understand English. That's sometimes useful for us to know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To a certain extent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stojanovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Maksimovic, please tell the Court whether at some point in time you provided a statement to General Mladic's Defence team in written form?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can we please have 1D01605 in e-court. Page 1, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, are the details contained in this first page correct and is this your signature?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us now go to the last page, please. Is the signature on the last page of the document yours? And the numbers 20/05/2014, is that in your own handwriting?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I were to put the same questions to you today that were put to you while preparing your statement and during proofing, having solemnly declared to speak the truth, would you remain with the statement you provided to General Mladic's Defence team in its entirety?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender the accompanying documents with this statement, 65 ter numbers 1D02052.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you tendering the statement or the associated exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First the statement and then the associated exhibits, Your Honour. I apologise. First I'd like to tender 1D1605.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, no objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: No objections. No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D1605 receives number D547, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D547 is admitted into evidence. And I hasten to add to that, Mr. Stojanovic, that it seems that due to the colour of the copying that for this statement, again, and that apparently the cover page and the last page, the signature page, have been separated once because they are totally different in colour as far as copying is concerned. The ERN numbers -- the -- therefore, I would again, if you separate those parts of a document I would insist in the future that not only the first and the last page are signed but that the other pages are initialed as well, and once the statement is complete that you also attach a complete translation. I can see on the signature page that the witness signed for five pages, but that, for example, doesn't appear in the English version. Now not dramatic at this moment but a very careful and accurate handling of documents is, as we know by now, an absolute requirement. Associated exhibits. You mentioned one already, that was, I think 1D1 --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will repeat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 1D -- well, there is no need. 1D02052.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do object to this map. It's a street map which lacks clarity, and, upon reflection, does seem to confuse and mislead with respect to the area involved. So we would object to this associated exhibit at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have a look at it. And could you meanwhile, Mr. Stojanovic, respond to the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. I believe that that is not correct and that the witness marked the positions on this map, according to his best recollection, positions of his unit and position of two features that are referred to in our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, whether he marked anything or do you want to say that he confirmed pre-marking -- unless the witness did it himself. Witness, could you have a look at the screen. Those red oval signs and the lines, did you mark that yourself or was it marked for you and did you state it? Did you state about those markings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This map was presented to me in the Karadzic case and I marked the positions of my unit. And in the depth two features or rather two villages. In the technical sense, I don't know whether I actually made the markings or not, but this does represent what I know about that part of the territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, is your problem that you disagree with the markings in the statement? Because you said it did not -- it was unclear and vague and ...

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We've two objections. First is: I'm not sure I understood the answer when the witness indicated that in the technical sense he does not know whether he made the markings or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I take it that he wants to say that he, not himself, did not put those red ovals or the red line on that map but that it was done either upon his instruction or without his instruction but that he stated or testified about it. That is how I understood his testimony. And the witness nods to confirm that at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Second, Your Honour, looking at the map itself we obviously have had a number of maps presented with respect to the area of Sarajevo and around Sarajevo. This is a street map which is very confusing in light of the actual topography and the various areas that are at issue with respect to this map. And that would bear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you be a bit more concrete? I mean, it looks very much as a -- as an extract of a map we have seen very often before. Or is there anything ...?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Well, one of the confusing aspects, Your Honour, is a place that is very much at issue is referred to as Sharpstone. With respect to this particular area, which does not appear to be reflected on the map, and that appears to be what -- part of the substance of this witness's testimony would be about that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Typically seems to be a matter which, if he marked it in this way, you can further test those markings during cross-examination, I would say. I do not see anything in the map itself apart from you would have wished, perhaps, some features to be found more explicitly. The objection is overruled. Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D2052 receives number D548, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Any other associated exhibits, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, two more. I'm going to read both of them: 65 ter numbers 1D02053 and 1D02054.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, no objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D2053 receives number D549. And document 1D2054 receives number D550, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both are admitted into evidence. I see that in the statement of the witness the Mladic 65 ter numbers are used, so therefore we don't have to pay further attention to the Karadzic exhibit numbers unless you would want to further explore the Karadzic statement on the matter. In that case, Ms. Bibles, you should clearly state on the record that what 65 ter number in this case corresponds with the 65 ter number and -- oh, the exhibit number in the Karadzic case. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honours, I would like to read the summary of the statement. Witness Sinisa Maksimovic in the course of the war carried out a series of establishment and superior duties at the Sarajevo front, starting as a signals officer at the signals platoon at the SRK command, duties in the Intervention Platoon in the Igman Brigade, and company commander in the 1st Romanija Brigade in Mrkovici and in the Igman Brigade. He took part in the fighting at Igman in the summer of 1993 when the Army of Republika Srpska occupied positions of the Brezovaca facilities and the Tresnido Brdo [phoen] trig point from which the B&H army fired from their artillery weapons at positions of the VRS and at civilian buildings in Hadzici. After reaching an agreement with UNPROFOR, the VRS withdrew from this position because the UNPROFOR was supposed to take them over and keep them under their control. However, he witnessed a deception on this point because immediately after the VRS withdrew from this feature, it was captured or taken over by the B&H Army. Similar situation where the B&H Army and UNPROFOR acted together occurred during the NATO bombing in late August and in September 1995. UN Rapid Intervention Forces from positions of the B&H Army and together with them with aerial support from -- fired from artillery weapons of the highest calibre and range at positions of the VRS at which time their command post was struck, the witness's command post. This witness was also an eye-witness of artillery fire by the B&H army with 120- and 82-millimetre mortars and from howitzers at Ilidza. The witness is familiar with positions of the VRS and the B&H Army in the section of Spicasta Stijena and Grdonj hill because with his company he held the position in the forest on the slopes of Grdonj hill. The vantage point and the highest trig point of Grdonj hill was held by forces of the B&H Army who had a good vantage point over that part of town as well as Spicasta Stijena, the peek of which was held by the VRS. Neither his nor the neighbouring units at the time when he was in the area had any sniper weapons, and knowing this terrain in connection with incident F16 from the indictment, the witness asserts that the VRS positions were over 1.000 metres away from where the incident took place. Your Honours, that would be the summary and now I'm going to put some questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I suggest you do that after the break. We take a break and we resume at 20 minutes past midday after the witness has left the courtroom. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 20 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are waiting for the witness to come into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the interpreters have a correction. At the end of the previous session Mr. Stojanovic actually said that he has no questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means that Ms. Bibles can start her cross-examination right --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- after the arrival of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Maksimovic, since Mr. Stojanovic has no further questions for you, you'll now be cross-examined by Ms. Bibles. You'll find her to your right. And Ms. Bibles is counsel for the Prosecution. Ms. Bibles, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Maksimovic.

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Maksimovic, I would first like to start with a few questions about the statement that has been prepared for this case, for the Mladic case. First, could you tell us how many days you were interviewed in preparation for this statement?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand whether you mean preparations in The Hague or the total preparations for my testimony?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Preparation prior to your arrival at The Hague in preparation for signing your statement.

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: I think that it was in April 2013, that was the first time. Then twice in October, and then again in December. That was the last time. In 2013.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Did you review a draft statement on any of those dates?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Each time I would come to prepare, I would be shown what I had said and then corrections were made, whether everything was all right or not. The last time when I received my complete statement, I made handwritten corrections, I sent it back, and then I received the final version of my statement, I signed it, and that's the statement that we just looked at.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right. If we could direct attention to the fourth page of your statement under the section that has a bold "F16." I would like you to take a look at that when it comes up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And that would be D547.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Could you please take a look. As we see F16, there is one sentence, and then there is a paragraph that begins -- could you please carefully read that first sentence?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: To read it out loud? "About an alleged sniper-related incident on the 6th of March, 1995, from Spicasta Stijena towards Sedrenik."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Great. And just the line below that, could you read it to yourself and tell me whether it's accurate?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: I suggested this also the last time that I read it. I was actually not the company commander in this period and this is what is missing at the beginning of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, I'm sorry, could you clarify for us whether you were or were not the commander of the company on the 6th of March, 1995?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: I was transferred to the Igman Brigade in 1994 in the month of December so that I was not there at that period, but I did speak about this incident because I was familiar with the terrain. At the beginning of the paragraph what is missing is that "although during this period I was not the commander of the company."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: So just to be clear, you meant to say that you were not the commander of the company in who --

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: During that period.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Okay. So is it true then that you have no direct or personal knowledge of events which occurred in that -- the zone of that company on the 6th of March, 1995?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: None that would be direct or personal. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now at the top of this section, it's titled "F16," do you know what is meant by F16?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: I think that is a marking from the indictment, the marking that somebody allocated to an incident that is in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: In the Karadzic case a similar paragraph of your statement began with: "It has been explained to me that 6 March, 1995, a sniper incident also allegedly occurred." Could you tell us what was explained to you about the 6 March 1995 incident prior to the Karadzic statement?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: I was shown photographs from the place where the incident took place. I was shown the supposed place where the projectile was fired from. I was just talking about the units' positions and the possibility or impossibility of firing from that position.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And who did you have this discussion with?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: There was somebody there from the Defence team. I think it was Sladojevic. He was a member of Mr. Karadzic's Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'd now like to move to paragraph 5 of D547.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And I'd like to ask you a question about paragraph 5 of your Mladic statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: While this comes up on the screen, I would just like to ask the witness about F16. If I understood you correctly, in March 1995 you were not the commander of the company in whose zone of responsibility that specific position was on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Why did you sign this statement with this mistake?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I spoke responsibly about the unit's positions and the possibility due to the distance of whether it was possible to shoot or not. So it was my subjective opinion about the possibility of firing, and it was my assumption that this incident, just like many other incidents, could have happened because of a stray bullet or something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is not my question. I asked you why did you sign this statement with this mistake in relation to your command or not being in command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was an oversight on my part. In the final version of my statement, I did correct a few errors but that one I missed, so it was only when I came to The Hague in the proofing I drew Mr. Stojanovic's attention that this word is missing, not that at that period I was not the commander. That's the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Then I state for the record that during examination-in-chief this correction was not mentioned. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, directing your attention to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I could --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue on this item, I'm perhaps also addressing the Defence. Apparently in this part of the statement something is filled in: "Although during this period /I/ was the commander of the company." I wonder where the "I" comes from because the "although" suggests that there is knowledge despite not being in command over there. The "although" is otherwise unexplainable, and therefore I would invite the parties to review and to see whether there may be any -- any explanation in the original text which, of course, I cannot read myself, but at least it is suggested that the "I" does not clearly appear in the original one but textually we'll have to look at it. Ms. Bibles, because it now becomes so much of a focus that we should pay proper attention to it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Perhaps we should go back to the section of F16.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Maksimovic, in reading the B/C/S sentence, the first sentence that has to do with the command of this unit. In B/C/S does it indicate the subject of command, who it is, whether it's you or someone?
