Is it -- I guess what I'm asking is: Is this sentence - this first sentence - in B/C/S grammatically correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What -- yes, we could ask the witness, but, as a matter of fact, I announced that we should ask experts in language rather than --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I do not mind if the witness answers the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, did you have a look at your original? Could you tell us whether in the third line of where we read F16, whether it's -- as far as you are concerned, it's clear who was in command of the company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Serbian language this sentence is confusing, because it says "although during this period was the commander of the company," so it's nonsense. Although the sentence should state, "Although during this period I was," or "I was not the commander of the company." I felt that this was a typing error, and I did draw Mr. Stojanovic's attention to this when we spoke about it at the hotel. I didn't think that it would create any major problems, but I can here clarify now that from my entire statement it is evident that I was not at that command post throughout that whole period. And so this sentence should correctly state: Although during this period I was not the commander of the company. I think it's a grammatical error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now you have drawn the attention of Mr. Stojanovic to that error?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, what did you do with that information?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is correct, Your Honours. I felt that based on the contents of the paragraph that you can see in front of you, you can clearly see that it is contradictory because later in the same --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- paragraph it says December 1994 until the end --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I'm going to stop you there. Another puzzle for the Chamber where a witness clearly draws your attention to what he considers to be a mistake and you leave it as it is and you leave it to us then to read everything in context and then find the month of December and then have to conclude that there was a mistake, whereas the witness is clear that he has drawn your attention to it. It's coming closer and closer to malpractice, Mr. Stojanovic. Please be aware of that. Ms. Bibles, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Going back now to paragraph 5 of your statement, I just want to clarify a matter and it would be the -- unfortunately the bottom of page 2 and the top of page 3 in the English. Here you indicate that you completed your officer education on 26 June, 1992, and were appointed company commander at Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 1992 or 1994, Madam Bibles?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: 1992, Your Honour. Or, I'm sorry, 1994. You're absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do you stand by that statement in this -- in your Mladic statement?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Maksimovic, the reason that I asked that question is that in paragraph 4 of your signed Karadzic statement --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Which perhaps we could take a look at 1D02051, paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: -- you suggest or say that you finished your education on the 26th of June, 1994, and became the company commander in Mrkovici on 27 July, 1994. Is that -- which of the two statements is more correct with respect to when you became the company commander?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: I can say this: After I completed my education, I had about 20 days of time that I spent at the command of the 1st Romanija Brigade until I was transferred. I cannot give you the exact date when I came to Mrkovici. I cannot remember it. I cannot remember what day it was. While waiting to be transferred, I and the chief of staff of the 1st Romanija, we toured some positions including the battalion command, the company command at Mrkovica. It was summer. I don't know whether it was already July. I couldn't really tell you precisely. So after the last tour with the chief of staff, I was told that I would be transferred to that company.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Who did you take over for? Who was the prior company commander that you replaced?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: The person that I replaced was Mr. Blasko Rasevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'd next like to clarify some of your military experience that may be relevant to this case.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could go back to D547 and paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Paragraph 1 of your statement describes that prior to the war you lived in Blazuj, Ilidza municipality. Were you a member of the Territorial Defence for Blazuj?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: No. In 1991, in September, I began serving my regular military service with the JNA Prokuplje, the Republic of Serbia. Until the 15th of May, 1992, I stayed there when I was returned together with a number of other soldiers to Lukavica. In other words, I had no occasion to be a member of any other armed forces save for the regular JNA. Upon arrival in Lukavica, I stayed with the signals unit. There was a radio relay station near the SRK command and we as soldiers maintained communication between the Main Staff and the SRK command. It was at Trdomici [phoen] hill nearby. After that, I asked to be reposted to my native town of Blazuj. I was indeed sent there and joined the unit comprising my friends, neighbours, and family members. I accompanied them to the lines we held at the very beginning of the war. I'm not sure I discussed it here, but I can tell you that we held the lines at the foot of Igman at the same or about the same altitude as the quarry. After that sometime in --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll go through the relevant portions with you. And I just wanted to clarify then, in paragraph 2 when you say that you were reassigned to the SRK, this is the reassignment you're talking about from your mandatory service to the SRK?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And then you've described that you requested a transfer to the Igman Brigade. Do you know when the Igman Brigade was created?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do you know approximately?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: You see, sometime during May 1992 combat activities began and some units came into being; thus, I never inquired particularly about this one. I really can't say when it was established.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do you know if it was formed from the Blazuj Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so, because in Blazuj there was a JNA barracks. I think the unit was formed from JNA members, at least those who stayed. And then all other available men from the settlement itself joined.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now in paragraph 2 you describe that Dunjic was the commander of your unit. Was this Major Velimir Dunjic?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. At some point of time he commanded a brigade. I don't know whether he was already in command when I joined the Igman Brigade or afterwards, but I do know that he was one of the commanders who together with me and my unit participated in certain combat activities. That is the period I remember him from.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Is it true that the Igman Brigade was one of the smallest brigades in the SRK?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could see 65 ter 30877.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, this is a combat readiness report for the Igman Light Infantry Brigade for the first half of 1993. Do you see the description in the upper left side of the report on the state of combat readiness?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And I can tell you that it's signed by Lieutenant-Colonel Cojic. Would you like to look at the last page on the signature line?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: No need. I do recall Lieutenant-Colonel Cojic. I recall his last name although we never met. Since so much time has elapsed, I don't remember him particularly well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could go to page 4 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: While this is coming up, in the fist line of paragraph 3 of your statement, you state: "I became a member of the Igman Brigade Intervention Platoon with the 4th Battalion in January 1993." Now turning your attention to page 4 here, we see a listing of the units that comprise the Igman Brigade in 1993. And I have a question about which unit you were a part of. Were you a part of the 4th Infantry Battalion or were you part of, down at the bottom, the Independent Intervention Company?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: My unit belonged to the 4th Infantry Battalion in Blazuj. I'm not aware of this other unit you referred to.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: While we're on page 4, just below the listing of these units is a description of several brigade facilities which require manpower from the brigade. I want to ask you about four of these. There is the Hadzici maintenance and repair depot, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you sure that we have the corresponding page on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Let's see. Ah, no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We don't. Let's see. The English is correct, so I believe we need to go perhaps back, if I remember everything correctly, on the B/C/S. No. I'm sorry. We need to go to page 5 in B/C/S. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Does that make more sense?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Now, then, going below the list that we were just asking about, I want to just ask a couple of questions about these four facilities: The Hadzici maintenance and repair depot; the Zunovnica ammunition depot; and then barracks in Blazuj; and is it Usivak? Are these all within the area of responsibility of the Igman Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: In paragraphs 3 and 4 of your statement, you describe ABiH fire on Hadzici and Ilidza. Were these four locations some of the targets of that fire?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: You see, as for Hadzici, in addition to the military facilities you mentioned, the targets were all over the place. Hadzici is so situated that it was exposed to shell fire, machine-gun fire from higher up incessantly and randomly it seems to me. Specifically, the way I see that shelling of Hadzici and Ilidza, I could not observe that one of these facilities was hit in a particular moment in time. I only know that both soldiers and civilians were often injured by fire coming from Igman. Somewhere in my statement I mentioned it. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'd like to go back to talking about the intervention unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: But before I move on, I tender 65 ter 30877.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30877 receives number P6630, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6630 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Is it true that around the 31st of August, 1993, there was a substantial reorganisation of the Igman Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Please clarify.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your statement explains that in September of 1993 you went to the officer school in Banja Luka. Isn't it correct that at that same time three intervention companies in the Igman Brigade were eliminated?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I do recall that when I left the Intervention Platoon of the 4th Battalion, shortly afterwards the Intervention Platoon was disbanded and the soldiers moved to other units. But that was not my personal experience. I only heard about it because by that time I had already gone to Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Perhaps it would be helpful to look at the order reorganising the brigade for the next few questions. That would be 65 ter 30889.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, sir, while this comes to our screen, this was signed by Colonel Cojic on 31 August, 1993. And again, can you see the upper left-hand side where it lists the subject of this order?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do you have any need to see the last page or the signature page of this order before we go through it in more detail?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Turning to page 2 in both version, hopefully, we'll look at point 6, and we see that it states: "On 1 September, 1993, the following unit shall cease to exist:" And it lists three intervention companies. The T or the Tomo Veljancic Intervention Company, the Hadzici Intervention Company, and the Blazuj Intervention Company. Which one of these intervention companies were you a member?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: The Blazuj Intervention Platoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Were you familiar with the other two intervention companies?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: I'm aware of them. I knew some people who were members of those units. Perhaps not very closely, though.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Turning to page 3 at point 7 in both versions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- before it disappears from the screen, I ask

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We saw in the document a reference to the Blazuj Intervention Company. Your answer was in relation to the Blazuj Interference Platoon. Was it a platoon or a company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a platoon. It had between 25 and 30 people, maybe even less. But, in any case, it was no company but a platoon and it belonged to the 4th Blazuj Battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And there was no Blazuj Intervention Company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] None that I know of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Because we see this term in this document, which we have in front of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But could I -- in addition to that, I see two times the word "ceta" and one time the word "vod," where apart from that I see also on the first line "the brigade," which seems not to be translated or at least -- could you slowly read the three lines aloud? Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Item 6 you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. To start at the second line and then to read the second, third, and fourth line of that paragraph. So starting with "interventa ceta," that's where I -- yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The intervention company of the Tomo Veljancic Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next line would be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Hadzici Intervention Company and the Blazuj Intervention Platoon. Those three units existed as part of the Igman Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That seems to resolves the matter. Could the -- I don't know who prepared this translation, but at least we would like to have it reviewed and to be made more accurate. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And then turning to page 3 at point 7, we read that: "The T. Veljancic Intervention Company, the Hadzici Intervention Company, and the Blazuj" -- well, I'm going to call it a platoon for now, "Intervention Platoon, have made a vast contribution through their work so far and their struggle for the freedom of the Serbian people and the forming of Republika Srpska. "I wish all members of these units good health and good luck in combat in the new units of the VRS." Did you receive a personal commendation for your work in the Intervention Platoon in -- that would be consistent with this -- this statement?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: To be honest, I don't recall it because I went to Banja Luka for schooling. I don't know whether my colleagues received this. I probably did not, otherwise I would be able to recall it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, going to the first intervention company, the Tomo Veljancic Intervention Company, do you know if the members of that company were local or if they came from outside the SRK?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: I think there was a number of locals in that company's structure. I don't know how it was structured, though. But there were mainly young guys who were fearless. For the most part in such intervention units, the personnel was young. In terms of each of these units' structure, I'm not aware of it. I know that in addition to us, the locals in the Intervention Platoon, there were also some refugees from the federation, from the district of Zenica and from Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, actually, if we could go back to page 2 just below point 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We see there that with respect to the Tomo Veljancic Intervention Company, you see subsection a, you see that they are being disbanded and that members from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia are being sent back to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. So do you have any idea how many men of that company may have come from the FRY?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know how many came from the FRY. But I do know there were several. I'm not certain of the figure, but I don't think there were all too many.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Are you aware whether the units' commander was known as Branislav Gavrilovic or Brne?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Branislav Gavrilovic, aka, Brne. That was the name of that unit's commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I move on, I would tender 30889.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30889 receives number P6631, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Before you continue, Ms. Bibles, I would like to hear from the parties whether they wanted to discuss the scheduling issues at the end of this session or early in the next session. I don't know where we stand at this moment, whether there is already something to be discussed or whether you would still need the next break.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I could use next break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then perhaps it's better to wait --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- until after the break. Yes, please proceed Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Maksimovic, do you know whether that unit was organised by the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not personally aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Were you aware that Gavrilovic had received weapons from the Republika Srpska police?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: No. I can only discuss what I know from personal experience. Probably something may have said something of the sort, but I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right. Well let's take a look at a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, is that to establish that those weapons were actually provided by or received by?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: It's the nature of the weapons with respect to what that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: -- the giving of the weapons would signify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean, if the witness doesn't know anything about it, it's no need to further educate him on these kind of matters so that he would learn what may have happened. If you have any useful questions to put to him in this context, of course you are free to do so, but sometimes there is a tendency of telling the witness what he doesn't know nevertheless is true which is not something which the Chamber would encourage.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Maksimovic, is it -- was it an average thing or a normal thing for pistols to be issued to soldiers or TO members by the police?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can see here, the date is the 11th of April, 1992. And I'm trying to recall when one might call "normal" at the time. I'm trying to figure out whether it was according to procedure or not. It was at the beginning of the war, and speaking from this place now I would say that it was probably not a correct thing to do. But at the time it may well have been. But then, that's my personal view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, normality is not really a factual issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We'll move away from this document for the time being. Were you aware in 1992 that Gavrilovic's units trained a number of Serbian volunteers who fought in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: What was your understanding of the reputation of Gavrilovic?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, at the very beginning of the war, I remember him enjoying the reputation of an intrepid soldier surrounded by a very strong team. There were no particular rumours, but he was just known as someone who did something at a certain point in time which provided him with a certain reputation in my mind and in the mind of others in terms of his warriorship, so to speak. That's all. But there's nothing more that I could say in particular.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: You prefaced your answer with "at the beginning of the war." Did you come to learn more about his reputation or did his reputation change throughout the course of the war?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please be a bit more specific as to changed in what way.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'll go to some very specific questions. But first I'll check the time. In paragraph 3 of your statement you explain that you took part in an operation in 1993. Was that also referred to as Lukavac 93?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Were you aware that Gavrilovic and his men also took part in this operation?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Did his unit work in co-operation or co-ordination with your intervention unit or platoon?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Were you aware that Gavrilovic's unit took prisoners during this operation?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, his unit and my unit both had prisoners specifically in that fight.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do you know whether Gavrilovic's men murdered prisoners in this operation?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. All I know is that we handed our prisoners over to the brigade command -- or, rather, the military police escorted them. We're talking about three soldiers who were a Serb, a Croat, and a Muslim by ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about what happened to prisoners that had been taken by Gavrilovic and his men?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: I think that they were also handed over to the brigade command, but I don't know that personally. All I know is that the soldiers that we had captured were handed over for interrogation. I don't know what happened to them later. One of those prisoners I know was called Pero. I cannot remember his last name. I know that he actually switched sides. From our side he switched to the B&H army. I don't know where that was.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I think you're referring to -- I'm sorry. You're referring to one of your prisoners or a prisoner of your platoon?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I put --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- a question. Do I have to understand that Pero was part of your army and you arrested him as a prisoner before he switched over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. He was a member of the B&H Army. He was captured and then taken to the brigade command, but then a few years later, perhaps, I heard that he escaped. I don't know where and when. I wouldn't be able to say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So he was not switching over from your army. He just escaped as a prisoner and went to the BiH.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, I'm looking at the clock. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom. We would take a break of 20 minutes, Mr. Maksimovic. And meanwhile, Ms. Bibles, you thought it would be helpful to look at the order reorganising the brigade for a few questions. You referred to it by 65 ter 30889 but that is now admitted as P6631. That's one. The other, the translation issue about "companies" or "platoons," would it be the Prosecution who will submit the translation for review and revision?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We'll do so, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we take a break and will resume at 20 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to give an opportunity to the parties to address the Chamber on scheduling issues. Where are we at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles and I worked hard today on this issue and I think that we reached the agreement at the end. And, Your Honours, would you like me just to send you a list or you want me to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you -- if you are in agreement --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- then the Chamber is -- it's unlikely that the Chamber would intervene in any way and then we would like to receive a list.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has the matter of 92 ter, 92 bis also been resolved for the two witnesses with the same name?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We removed them from that list --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- for testimony for the next period. So we'll sort it out somehow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you still can consider how to deal with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So -- and are the parties also committed to avoiding chaos and to try to really finalise the scheduled testimony within the time-limits. I want the realistic approach; that's one. And sometimes we may lose 10 or 15 minutes. But the Chamber is not expecting the parties to lose 30 or more minutes just on nothing, on chaos and unclarity. I take it that you have considered that as well and that you are expected to be realistic approach.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have attempted to estimate as best we can given the variables --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: -- our testimony. Our concern is obviously going up against the recess we would not want a witness postponed over the course of the recess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And we may come a little short based on our estimates --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: -- but right now it looks -- it looks very solid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the Chamber would like to receive a list with the times and the dates. And to use our time as efficiently as possible to ask the witness to be escorted into the courtroom now right away. I asked that the witness be escorted into the courtroom right away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Maksimovic, Ms. Bibles will now continue her cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Maksimovic, to finish the area that we were discussing prior to the break, you mentioned a prisoner who you knew named only Pero. Was that the first name? You nodded.

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I don't know if his first name was that or if it was his nickname. I really couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If I suggested a last name of Koblar, would that refresh your recollection at all?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: It's possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: It's possible his name was Pero Koblar?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 30888 brought to the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Maksimovic, this is a statement given by Pero Koblar. I'll ask you to look at the identifiers in the top of the first page, please. Now you -- prior to the break, you also described that he escaped, and you see in the introduction line here that part of his statement has to do with an escape. Does this appear to be same individual that you were describing prior to the break?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Very probably, yes. Perica Koblar, yes, I think that that was his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 8 in the English and page 9 in the B/C/S. If we look at -- I believe it's the bottom of the page in the English version and the top of the page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Koblar describes being questioned in Gavrilovic's presence. Do you see that reference at the top of the page 9 in the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And then down below he describes, without going into the entire paragraph -- but one of Gavrilovic's men on the left of Gavrilovic, or known by Brne, asked a prisoner named Zika in which operations he had participated. And Zika answered 11 -- I think it's Plavih, the soldier raised his AP and fired a burst on Zika. So my question to you is: Were you aware of this unit murdering prisoners during this operation?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of this. After capturing Golo Brdo, my unit immediately received the assignment to go to the right to Stupnik. The action was still underway so then we continued on our way. Once we captured those trig points, we heard about fierce infantry fighting that was being waged behind our back, practically. This is what we heard and we received information that our unit, which had taken up the line at Golo Brdo, had been attacked by the B&H army and that they were holding up well. So we went in that direction. So I definitely don't know anything about these other things here.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now you -- you had heard about a Pero and you now believe that is this individual, Mr. Koblar. How did you hear about Pero Koblar?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know now whether that was while he was actually taken prisoner. I don't know. I didn't capture him. I don't know which of the men did it. I found out that one of them was called Pero. It kind of leaked among the soldiers. Somebody took him. I don't know who it was. And then when we consolidated our lines, we went to our next assignment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to dispute the account of the murder that you read here in Mr. Koblar's statement?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't read the entire statement. I see the beginning here. I have nothing to say definitely about it. I cannot talk about things that I don't know anything about.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: It appears we will not finish with your testimony today. Would you agree to take this statement with you over the weekend, it is a rather long statement, but to see if that assists you any in assessing this -- this information?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: It's not a problem at all. I can read it. You mean you would like me to state my view about the truthfulness of the statement? Of course, it's something that I cannot do, but I can read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I would ask you to read the whole statement and then I may have some additional -- or I would have some additional questions for you on Monday. So we can --

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We can move on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Will you provide the witness with the statement during this hearing, or would he receive it through the intervention of the Victims and Witness Section?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: The -- we can print this out at the conclusion of the court session and give it to the court usher to give to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, first, give it for inspection to the Defence and then give it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's proceed as you suggest. Please proceed now.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Well, we'll shift directions and go back to some more details in your statement. From the 20 -- well, sometime in the summer of 1994 to December 1994, you were in the 1st Romanija Brigade of the SRK and you've described that you were the company commander at Mrkovici. And that's described in paragraphs 5 through 9 of your statement. In paragraph 6 you describe information that you had received about something that occurred in February of 1994. I want to be very clear that you were not in the 1st Romanija Brigade in February of 1994?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And it's correct that you were not anywhere near Sarajevo, actually, on the 5th of November, 1994?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: I was not near Sarajevo, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: So it's true, isn't it, then, that you have no direct or personal knowledge of the events of the 5th of February, 1994, about Markale market?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't have any personal knowledge. I know only what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could go to D547.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And look at the end of paragraph 5 in your statement. With respect to your area of responsibility as company commander of the Mrkovici Company of the 1st Romanija Brigade, is it accurate to say that your area of responsibility did not extend back actually to the village of Mrkovici or Radava?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: The villages of Mrkovici and Radava were in the depth of the territory. Members of my unit were actually the inhabitants of those two villages. The area of responsibility encompassed, if I can remember correctly now, about 12 trenches or so belonging to my unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please go to the next page in English. We wanted to see the last part of paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Am I reading your answer correctly, that your area of responsibility in this position was -- would this have been the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand you quite, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your -- you've just testified at line -- well, now 84, starting at line 13: "The area of responsibility encompassed, if I can remember correctly now, about 12 trenches or so belonging to my unit." Can you describe to us what that means?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: These were points of resistance in a connected system of defence. It was my company's responsibility to take care of those 12 or 13 trenches that were linked with cross-trenches. They were well fortified and of key importance to the villages of Mrkovici and Radava and the part of Republika Srpska that was ours, Blazuj, Hadzici, Ilidza. The road connecting those parts with the rest of Republika Srpska actually passed not far from the lines that were covered by my unit. It was about some 50 or a bit more, a hundred metres as the crow flies, between our main road and the front line. The trenches were well fortified. In the depth of the territory, if you allow me to explain - meaning the villages of Mrkovici, Radava, what else, Mocevci [phoen] - that's where these villages were.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now moving to page 4 of your statement in the section below F16, you describe adjoining units in a way that's a little confusing. So I'd like to go over those again to see if I understand. You used in this section --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And this would be in both versions the third full paragraph down that begins with, "I further want to specify ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: You describe the adjoining units based on left or right. Is it all right with you if we go through these and try instead of using "left" and "right" to use "west" or "east" of your position at -- at the line at Mrkovici? So from your position at Mrkovici, let's first go west. From your position in the 1st Romanija Brigade there going west, wasn't the next unit over the Kosevo Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: The Vogosca Kosevo Battalion. It was mostly the Kosevo Battalion; that's putting it more precisely. Up there we refer to that unit as the Vogosca Brigade because we were practically the last unit in the 1st Romanija that had a neighbour to the right, another larger unit that was not directly part of it. That's to the west.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And then actually further west from Kosevo -- the Kosevo area, would actually be the Vogosca Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: I think that it was all one unit. Perhaps it was the 4th Sarajevo Brigade. I -- I don't know exactly. I'm not sure how it was called. I think it was called the 4th Sarajevo Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Could it have -- I'm sorry. Could it have been the 3rd?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Reading your statement, it seems that you're familiar with a location known as Spicasta Stijena, which was also known as Sharpstone. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And is it true that with the exception of one night and maybe a couple of days in 1994, this location was held by the VRS from 1992 to 1995?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We or the VRS held positions there with some brief interruptions. On several occasions, those positions were taken by the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Is it correct that Sharpstone, this location, is an elevated point which allows good views of the eastern part of the city of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: There is a good view from the feature of the village of Sedrenik and further afield towards the city of Sarajevo itself. However, it was not the highest trig point in the area of responsibility, or at least not in that part.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Okay. But -- but the primary point, I guess, is what you could see from Sharpstone. And I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness has --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: -- you have answered that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- answered that question, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, despite the fact that you have no personal knowledge of the incident on the 6th of March, 1995, or F16, I would like to ask a couple of questions about the more general comments that you made while discussing this incident in your statement. Now you -- in your statement, you've estimated a thousand metres between the Serbian positions and the victim's location. I'd like to ask you about that. Is it true that you were never provided the specific details of the location of the victim's location?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, the witness did not give an estimation. He said it was more than a thousand metres and he did not present that as an estimate but as knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Oh, I'll go back into that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And how did you come up with the distance of more than a thousand metres?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: I know the area and I also saw some photographs. My conclusion was that the distance was rather great. In the Karadzic case, the Defence team provided me with some photographs taken from Spicasta Stijena. There was information marked on them and it was stated that some of the incidents took place at a distance of over 1.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I intervene for a moment. Do I understand that you never measured specifically on a map or otherwise that distance and that it's just your conclusion based on your knowledge of the terrain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Specifically, I couldn't make any measurements because I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether you could or not, you didn't do it. That's what I'm asking you. Ms. Bibles, and I'm also looking at you, Mr. Stojanovic, it's of no use to further explore what in the view of a witness the distance would have been if there are maps. The only thing -- and even so, irrespective of whether the witness knew exactly where the victim was, it's just of no use as long as we have maps. So let's move on and listen to evidence which gives a better factual basis for whatever. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I was just clarifying that he had not -- he had not mapped this -- he had not taken other measures.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Maksimovic, one of the questions with respect to your statement in this particular area has to do with what you were trying to say about the weapons or the personnel who were available at Sharpstone. Now, I'll try to go to the core of the matter. Isn't it true that the SRK and the 1st Romanija Infantry Brigade did, in fact, have weapons and personnel who could fire with accuracy at or over a thousand metres?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: A unit such as a corps would probably have all assets available to it as envisaged by the establishment structure.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And again, you were not -- we've established that you were not in this company during any part of 1995 and would not have specific knowledge as to who or what equipment was present during that 1995 time-period?

utterances.speaker: SINISA MAKSIMOVIC
utterances.text: I was not a member of that unit, so I can't discuss it. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this point I would be shifting to another topic. I'm looking at the clock, and this may be a good time to rest for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll adjourn for the day, Mr. Maksimovic. We'd like to see you back on Monday, the 7th of July, at 9.30 in the morning. Ms. Bibles is aware that she has another 50 minutes available for cross-examination. I would like to instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way with whomever about your testimony whether already given or still to be given. Now, you will be provided with a copy of the statement. Has it been presented to the Defence already? Mr. Usher, could you please assist and show -- oh, is it printed out not yet? Or is there any problem with it? Do we have a ...

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: It's a long enough statement. Ms. Stewart was concerned about this so we're printing it out right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, when I said you had 50 minutes left I had forgotten that it was two and a half hours you announced rather than two hours, so even 80 minutes are left. Mr. Usher, could you assist and show to Mr. Stojanovic the document that is to be provided to the witness. Now, Witness, if I say you should not communicate with anyone about your testimony, that includes matters like what will be provided to you and that is an order of the Court. And that also means that if you would violate that order, that you are subject to, well, pretty heavy penalties in terms even of imprisonment of long duration. We'll wait for the statement to be printed out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that the statement is not 500 pages or something like that? No, no, that's now -- Mr. Usher, could you provide it to Mr. Stojanovic for inspection. Mr. Stojanovic, as an eye-witness I can assure you that no one added anything in writing on it, so if it is the document then -- Mr. Usher, could you please provide the witness with that statement. You have the whole of the weekend to read through it, Mr. Maksimovic. We highly appreciate that you are willing to spend your time on reading the statement. We would like to see you back Monday morning, 9.30. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day and will resume Monday, the 7th of July, 2014, in this same courtroom, I, at 9.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 7th day of July, 2014, at 9.30 a.m.
